pageCache.pageTitle: About | London Vocational Ballet School | LVBS
pageCache.text:
About LVBS
Empowering Minds and Inspiring Futures in London's Rich Cultural Landscape
A Warm Welcome from our Directors
At London Vocational Ballet School, we are dedicated to shaping the future stars of classical dance, providing them with a solid foundation that blends the artistry of ballet with a comprehensive academic education. Our commitment to excellence sets us apart as a premier vocational ballet establishment, where students thrive both as dancers and scholars.
Our mission is clear: to prepare aspiring dancers for the rigours of upper school ballet training, all while fostering their intellectual growth. Small class sizes lie at the heart of our approach, ensuring that every student receives personalised attention and tailored guidance.
From Year 6 to Year 11, we offer a comprehensive educational journey that focuses on the renowned British classical technique. For our younger aspiring dancers, our associate programme provides a stepping stone towards future excellence. Alongside these courses, our Holiday and Outreach courses offer the ability to experience the vocational training curriculum of the full-time program, delivered by our faculty alongside renowned guest tutors and live musicians.
One of our proudest achievements lies in our distinguished alumni, who have left an indelible mark on the performing arts industry. Their successes reflect the dedication, passion, and transformative education that define the London Vocational Ballet School experience.
Our school values, as chosen by our students and faculty are: Courage | Respect | Nurture | Resilience. We all endeavour as a school to embody these values in everything we do.
Whether your aspirations lie in the world of dance or you seek a holistic education that nurtures both body and mind, London Vocational Ballet School is your destination for excellence.
Welcome to London Vocational Ballet School.
Kate Blakeburn MA (Hons), Academic Director and Louise Bennett BA Artistic Director
Full-time School
Our full-time, co-educational school offers a dynamic blend of renowned vocational dance training and bespoke academic tuition.
With expert support from leading vocational dance practitioners and a host of guest coaches from the wider dance sector, our full-time programme ensures students achieve their ambitions
Associate Course
Our associate course feeds directly into the full-time school and offers students an introduction to LVBS's style of training in a safe, enjoyable environment. With several styles of dance incorporated into the once-weekly sessions, we try to ignite the creative spark in aspiring young dancers.
Holiday Courses
Our holiday courses give students from all over the UK the opportunity to join us for intensive periods of masterclasses and tuition, curated by us and delivered by leading industry figures alongside our faculty
STREAM
Our STREAM project is looking to partner with local academic schools as well as local dance schools to offer clearer pathways into vocational training for talented young people. Click here to learn more.
Faculty & Staff
Meet the team of experts delivering some of the finest vocational and academic training in London
Facilities and Location
In the heart of West London, London Vocational Ballet School is within touching distance of the Capital's wider cultural tapestry - the perfect setting to educate young artists
Curriculum
Academic outcomes are matched by exceptional vocational results at LVBS.
Term Dates and Fees
Learn more about the tuition fees and term dates for London Vocational Ballet School

pageCache.pageTitle: Summer Show Forces of Nature | London Vocational Ballet School | LVBS
pageCache.text:
London Vocational Ballet School are delighted to be returning to the Lilian Baylis Theatre, presenting Forces of Nature, an evening of diverse works curated by LVBS's Artistic Director Louise Bennett and performed by our talented dancers. Inspired by the beauty, strength and power of the natural world, the performance will celebrate our forces of nature - the young artists of LVBS.
The evening will include new works by Daniel Davidson, Bim Malcomson, Miguel Altunaga, Louise Bennett, Georgina McDermott, Megan Webster-Shaw, Brook Ogle, Patricia Okenwa, and the school's Founder and Honorary Patron Anna du Boisson OBE, alongside a revival of Louise Bennett's Flora, created for National Youth Ballet in 2019. This year also sees the introduction of the LVBS Young Choreographer Award, which supports a student to create and present a work, under the guidance of an industry professional. The evening promises to be a rich display of sparkling technique, ingenious creativity and beautiful ever-developing artistry!​​​​
Photography by: Jack Thomson

pageCache.pageTitle: STREAM | London Vocational Ballet School | LVBS
pageCache.text:
STREAM
Join our grassroots development project which encourages young people to explore artistic pathways and a vocational dance education
About the Project
STREAM has been born out of an ambition to bolster our community offering, further diversify our student body and also extend our reach as a leading ballet school and arts charity. STREAM takes our programme of study and delivers it to those who perhaps have not had the opportunity to experience a vocational training workshop before. We believe that by bringing high-quality delivery of dance education to places it would not normally touch, we can capture a much larger pool of talent in the South of England.
As part of this year's pilot delivery of STREAM, we are looking to partner with up to 15 academic schools, dance schools and after-school programmes to deliver workshops to students across the South of England, led by our experienced practitioners.
Exposure is key to this project. We know that by exposing young people to information about artistic pathways and working with them to explore what that type of educational journey can look like, it leads to greater engagement and an improved interest and appreciation for the arts, regardless of if the individuals desire to pursue the profession or not.
The skills honed in a vocational education with LVBS transfer directly into academic achievement. Discipline, problem solving and dedication underpin every sector of the modern world - these tools are the foundation of our teachings as part of our programme of study. In STREAM delivery, we touch on these as part of the information session post-workshop, allowing students to better understand the rigours of training as a ballet dancer and inspiring them to be fearless in pursuit of success.
What are the benefits of dance?
Increased muscular strength, endurance and aerobic fitness
Better coordination and agility
Improved spatial awareness
Increased overall physical confidence
Improved general and psychological well being
Greater self-confidence, self-esteem and self-motivation
Better social skills and mental dexterity
What will it encompass?
If you decide to apply to join us as a STREAM partner, we would facilitate a workshop for your students with movement and music, led by one of our faculty. We’d follow up our workshop with an information session, where we explore what training as a ballet dancer can look like, and identify the pathways towards pursuing dance as a career. We'll discuss the benefits of dance and debunk myths on following a career in the arts.
We are looking to do four key things with STREAM:
Develop a better understanding of the need for more projects like STREAM in the wider London area and the South of England
Encourage talent at a grassroots level and support it by demonstrating to young people the options available to them around a career in the arts
Diversify our student body and our associate programme
Build a network of “feeder” hubs into our LVBS Associate Programme and by, extension, our full-time school
Interested? Next steps...
Applications for partnership are open now. Please contact us here to discuss becoming a partner. If your application is selected, we will oversee the delivery of the initial workshop and provide you with resources to promote the project and your part in it.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum | London Vocational Ballet School | LVBS
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Explore the structure and delivery of our curriculum in greater detail
A Comprehensive Academic Week
At LVBS, we pride ourselves on offering an inclusive and personalised approach to education. Admission to the school is not contingent upon academic prowess. Upon joining us, students participate in academic assessments designed to identify their individual strengths and areas requiring improvement.
Our dedicated and highly qualified staff are committed to helping every student achieve their maximum potential. We maintain small class sizes to ensure that each student receives the support they need to make significant academic progress, regardless of their initial proficiency.​
London Vocational Ballet School offers a comprehensive academic curriculum, encompassing all core subjects such as English literature, foreign language, and mathematics. Our approach caters to students of varying abilities, offering both foundation and extended levels to accommodate individual learning needs.
In line with our commitment to holistic development, we place particular emphasis on Personal, Social, and Health Education (PSHE), as well as Relationships and Sex Education (RSE). Additionally, we focus on instilling modern British values and prioritising the mental and physical well-being of our students.
To ensure continuous growth, we diligently assess and record students' homework progress. Regular meetings and comprehensive reports are provided to keep parents informed about their child's academic journey. We firmly believe in the importance of individualised attention and support for each student's success.
Subject Delivery and Key Stages
Years 6, 7, 8 and 9 (Key Stage 3)
Science (Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Geography)
Years 10 and 11 (Key Stage 4) - Partially Selective
BTEC First Certificate in Performing Arts

Holiday Courses & Summer Masterclasses
At London Vocational Ballet School, our holiday courses and summer masterclasses are designed to give young dancers the opportunity to experience high-quality vocational training outside of term time.
Whether joining us for a structured multi-day course or a one day masterclass, students benefit from expert teaching, a focused learning environment, and the chance to develop technique, artistry and confidence.
Spring Steps Easter Course
Summer Masterclass 2026
Spring Steps Easter Development Course
A focused and immersive 4-day training experience designed to support technical and artistic development.
Delivered during the Easter holidays.
Full course booking (4 consecutive days).
Culminates in an informal sharing performance.
Designed for: Years 4–7 and Years 8–12.
Vocational training approach throughout.
Spring Steps offers students the opportunity to experience the structure and intensity of vocational training, while working towards a final performance outcome.
Summer Course Masterclass Series
A flexible programme of themed masterclasses delivered across the summer holidays.
Four individual masterclasses.
Each session can be booked separately.
Varied themes and teaching focus.
Designed for: Years 5–8 and Years 9–12.​
Ideal for students looking to explore different styles, refine specific skills, or experience LVBS training in a more flexible format.
Bookings are now open for our Summer Masterclasses 2026.
Photography by: Jules Renahan

pageCache.pageTitle: Support Us| Sponsorship & Partnership | London Vocational Ballet School | LVBS
pageCache.text:
Support the Future of Ballet At LVBS
Investing in the next generation of dancers
At London Vocational Ballet School, we train young dancers to the highest vocational standards, combining exceptional classical ballet training with a strong academic curriculum. We believe dancers should also be critical thinkers, problem-solvers and confident learners. Our students arrive with amazing potential and, with the right training, discipline and support, they progress to leading upper schools and professional pathways. But world-class vocational training comes at a cost and not every family can meet it alone.
Your support ensures that talent, dedication and promise, not financial circumstance determine a student’s future.
Why Your Support Matters
Vocational ballet training requires:
Academic provision alongside intensive dance training
Live musical accompaniment
Conditioning and strength training
Performance opportunities
Corporate Partnerships
Partnering with London Vocational Ballet School aligns your organisation with:
Excellence and discipline
Arts education and cultural investment
Social mobility through access to training
Community impact in West London
Support for young people at a pivotal stage in their development
We work collaboratively with sponsors to create partnerships that deliver both meaningful impact and brand value.
Opportunities include:
Production sponsorship
Capital project support
Long-term patronage programmes
If your organisation has CSR objectives aligned with arts, education, innovation or youth development, we would welcome a conversation.
From Potential to Professional
Our mission is to prepare students for full-time upper school training and beyond.
Through rigorous technical development, musicality and disciplined academic study, our students leave LVBS equipped not only for professional ballet pathways, but for excellence in any field they pursue. Over our history, we have nurtured young people who have progressed into upper schools, performing arts careers and academic achievement. Support ensures this pathway remains open to every talented child who earns their place.
Governance and Commitment
London Vocational Ballet School is committed to:
Safeguarding and student welfare
Equality, inclusion and diversity
Responsible governance
Financial transparency
We welcome conversations with individuals, trusts and foundations who wish to understand our impact in greater depth.
Support Us
Every pirouette mastered. Every audition secured. Every young dancer stepping closer to their dream.
These moments are made possible through belief and support.
